articles.title: When Fat Cells Fail: How Losing Adipose Tissue Can Trigger Diabetes
articles.summary: New research reveals that in a rare disease, fat cells undergo catastrophic changes—losing their ability to store lipids, becoming inflamed, and suffering mitochondrial failure. This breakdown disrupts metabolism, leading to diabetes. The findings highlight fat's crucial role as an active organ, not just passive storage.

articles.title: A Cellular Tipping Point: How Microglia May Determine Alzheimer's Resilience
articles.summary: A study in Nature Medicine reveals that microglia, the brain's immune cells, undergo a critical state change that may decide whether Alzheimer's pathology leads to dementia. Resilient individuals—including centenarians—show distinct microglial responses, offering new therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Fighting Fire with Fire: Prescribed Burns Save Giant Sequoias from Extreme Wildfires
articles.summary: A UC Davis study in Nature Communications shows prescribed burns dramatically boost giant sequoia survival during megafires. Trees in treated areas were four times more likely to survive the 2020-2021 fires. The research estimates 1,900 trees were saved, highlighting a critical conservation tool.
